title: Redesign a task to be AI-resilient
goal: Make a redesigned assignment AI can't quietly do for the student — you stay the designer.

blocks.title: Design smarter, not stricter
blocks.body:
You could police harder — ban phones, hover, run every essay through a detector. It's exhausting, and it treats every child as a suspect.

There's a kinder, stronger move: design the task so AI simply can't do the interesting part. Anchor it to something only your student has — this class, their own thinking, their voice, their process.

Let's redesign one real task you set. Pick what fits, and you stay the designer.

blocks.scaffold: Redesign this {{gradeBand}} {{subject}} [task] so it needs the student's own thinking, voice, or process. Anchor it to something AI can't supply — for example: an in-class writing step, a link to a specific lesson or local example we discussed, a draft-then-reflect stage, or a short oral 'walk me through it'. Keep it fair and doable in our classroom.

blocks.question: How usable is your redesigned task — could you set it next week?
